intervals.label: detector construction and installation
intervals.note: Start from the news item dated 2017.12; end is the first data taking (commissioning run, 2020-06-05).
intervals.quote: The part of the detector construction work is started at J-PARC.

intervals.label: commissioning run and refilling
intervals.note: First data on 2020-06-05, a 10-day commissioning run (5-15 June 2020, per arXiv:2111.07482); the detector was then refilled and re-installed in December 2020. End is the start of the first long physics run.
intervals.quote: We started to take data from June-5. The first physics run (the commissioning run) will be continued for 10 days.

intervals.label: long physics runs with the 24 m detector
intervals.note: First long run 2021-01-12 to June 2021; further long runs from 2022-01-28, spring 2023 and 2023-12-07 are listed on the same page. The Feb 2026 first-results paper says data taking is ongoing.
intervals.quote: In 2021-Jan, we start the first long term physics run (Jan-12).

website.quote: The first results on sterile neutrino search using 2022 data was published.

placements.note: Start: the news item says the detector was moved from the assembly building to the MLF on Feb-19 (item dated 2020; the year is inferred from the dated entry); it was re-installed on the 3rd floor in December 2020 after filling. The site point is the MLF building centroid (campus-grade).
placements.quote: employs a 50-ton liquid scintillator detector on the third floor of the MLF, at a baseline of 24 m from the neutrino source

fiducial_mass.note: Design value in the technical design report; stored as mass because the validator has no scintillator-volume key.
fiducial_mass.quote: The detector has a fiducial volume of 17 tons and is located 24 meters away from the mercury target.

pmt_count.note: As built (January 2020); the technical design report foresaw 193 8-inch PMTs.
pmt_count.quote: All of 120 PMTs were installed finally.

target_distance.quote: detector with 0.1 w% Gd concentration placed at 24 m from the target

total_mass.quote: The JSNS2 experiment employs a 50-ton liquid scintillator detector on the third floor of the MLF

summary.plain: The scintillator detector of JSNS2: a tank of gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator watched by light sensors, 24 metres from the mercury target of J-PARC's neutron source, built to catch the flash of an antineutrino striking a proton.
summary.technical: Liquid-scintillator detector: acrylic vessel with 17 t (fiducial) 0.1 % Gd-loaded scintillator, unloaded scintillator in the surrounding stainless-steel tank (about 50 t in all), 120 PMTs as installed; 24 m from the mercury target on the 3rd floor of the MLF.

technology.quote: The detector uses the Gd-loaded liquid scintillator, and oscillated anti-electron neutrinos are detected via the inverse beta decays
technology.value: Gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator in an acrylic vessel inside a stainless-steel tank, read out by photomultipliers; inverse beta decay with a delayed Gd neutron-capture signal
